To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the COMBINE global biogeochemistry model is able to reproduce the N 13C excursion observed in the Late Devonians, and 2) the model predicts a decrease in atmospheric CO2 from 2925 ppm before the Kellwasserevents, to 1560ppm after the Kellwaser events, which is in agreement with recent estimates of the Late Devonian pCO2.

the Frasnian/Famennian boundary carbon isotope excursion can be reproduced with the COMBINE climate-bio-geochemistry model by assuming that (1) a sea-level fall exposes platform carbonates to weathering, (2) the weathering of platform carbonate is responsible for the first part of the N 13C excursion (0.7x), (3) a rapid spreading of vascular plants on land increases the weathering of continental surface and the burial flux of organic matter,
(1) The Frasnian-Famennian (Kellwasser) events were caused by a rapid sea-level rise and a subsequent fall.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the global change of climate, sea level, and carbon isotope ratios across the Frasnial-Famennian boundary.
the Late Devonian, which was a time of global biotic crisis.
the Late Devonian, a time interval of great importance in Earth history.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Late Devonian perturbations in N 13C values and atmospheric pCO2 can only be explained by a combination of several mechanisms, including: 1) a global increase in the weatherability of the continental crust; 2) a decrease in the oceanic burial rate of organic carbon; 3) a change in the global phosphorus budget; 4) a change in atmospheric pCO 2.

a global warming of 4.4 C at the pole and of 2.1 C at the equator, a 30% increase of continental area colonized by land plants, a decrease of atmospheric pCO2 by 46.6%, an increase in phosphorus delivery to oceans by 40%, and a 20% increase of burial fluxes of organic matter are the most likely causes of the F-F boundary events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the F-F perturbations were caused by the sea-level rise, but that the sea-level rise itself was caused by a tectonic event.
the COMBINE modelling approach can be successfully applied to the Frasnian and Famennian, and provides a good framework to understand the Late Devonian climate and biogeochemical perturbations.

we have been able to model the global biogecochemical cycles of the F-F interval, and to identify the causes and timing of the large N 13C excursions, which are linked to the global climatic cooling and to the spread of land plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the F/F boundary was a time when the Earth system experienced rapid changes in climate, ocean circulation, and biogeochemistry, and these changes are all linked.

the Late Devonian perturbations in seawater N 14 C values are the result of a series of events that include: 1) sea-level rise, 2) stratification of the proto-Tethys ocean, 3) exposure of the continental shelf and weathering of platform carbonate, 4) spreading of vascular land-plants, 5) increase of continental weatherability and 6) increase of phosphorus supply to the ocean.

the Late Devonian global biogeochemistry was very sensitive to small changes in the global carbon cycle and climate, and that the F-F events can be explained by a simple scenario of continental weathering and burial of organic matter.
